simple.meaning: בְּשַׁר (bᵉshar) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “flesh.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Daniel 2:11. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בְּשַׁר (H1321) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H1321. besar בְּשַׂר noun masculine flesh ( בְּסַר ᵑ7 , Syriac ; Biblical Hebrew בָּשָׂר , √ בשׂר ); — absolute ׳ב Dan 7:5 flesh (as devoured by beast); emphatic בְּשְׂרָא 2:11 flesh = mankind, ׳כָּלבֿ 4:9 +?

occurrences.englishText: It is a rare thing that the king requires, and there is no other who can show it before the king, except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.”

“Belteshazzar, master of the magicians, because I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and no secret troubles you, tell me the visions of my dream that I have seen, and its interpretation.
“Behold, there was another animal, a second, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and three ribs were in its mouth between its teeth. They said this to it: ‘Arise! Devour much flesh!’
